mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (0.08%) compresses discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This signal is always active as it depends on the current level of the federal funds rate.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS is at or below 0.08%, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the CPI (Consumer Price Index) above 285.0 signals accelerating inflation, prompting market expectations of monetary tightening which depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 285.0, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When labor market tightness (PAYEMS > 150000) coincides with elevated inflation (CPIAUCSL > 285.0), the market anticipates aggressive monetary policy responses, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where PAYEMS > 150000 and CPIAUCSL > 285.0, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A late-cycle expansion regime, defined by high GDP growth (GDPC1 > 19800) and elevated housing starts (HOUST > 1600), signals overvaluation and impending economic cooling, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where GDPC1 > 19800 and HOUST > 1600, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (INDPRO > 103.0) indicates robust economic activity, supporting corporate earnings growth and reducing equity risk premiums, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This signal is always active as it depends on the current level of industrial production.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO > 103.0, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% signals a tight labor market, which typically precedes inflationary pressures and monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE < 3.5, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When labor market strength (PAYEMS > 150000) coincides with low unemployment (UNRATE < 3.5%), the market anticipates inflationary pressures and aggressive monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where PAYEMS > 150000 and UNRATE < 3.5, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A surge in housing starts above 1650.0 (HOUST > 1650.0) indicates strong consumer demand and potential overheating, which triggers market concerns about monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where HOUST > 1650.0, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
